correctness.rationale: For p=3 the source codifferential has a single multiplication map. Lemma 5.1(c) gives degree pair (1,1) at m=2 and (1,2) up to order at m=3. On an elliptic curve h0 equals positive degree. The m=2 product of two nonzero one-dimensional section spaces has rank 1. In m=3, multiplication by the unique nonzero section of the degree-one factor injects the two-dimensional section space of the degree-two factor, giving rank 2. The finite torsion marking does not alter rank, so source dimension m gives generic fiber dimension 1. The order-3 Hodge multiplicities are the same degree pairs; invariants in Sym^2 are precisely cross terms and have dimension ab=1 or 2, matching the computed ranks.

value.rationale: The source singles out p=3,m=2,3 as the only low-ramification cases not covered by its generic-finiteness theorem. Determining them exactly closes the natural boundary of that theorem: both fail by precisely one dimension. The invariant-tangent calculation further shows that this failure is geometrically forced by the order-3 endomorphism condition and that the family has maximal possible local variation subject to that condition. This is a structural boundary statement for the main moduli map of the paper, not an arbitrary numerical specialization.
